changes.after: Filter chooses which items stay, then map changes each chosen item into a result.

before: filter on a List keeps elements satisfying its Boolean predicate. map creates the transformed result values. These collection operations evaluate eagerly and do not mutate the original list. Here n names each lambda argument explicitly.

Keeping even values from 1, 2, 3, 4 leaves 2 and 4. Mapping each to ten times itself produces 20 and 40. The returned List exposes a read-only interface; read-only is not a universal guarantee of deep immutability.
Expected output or behavior: [20, 40]. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Swap the operation order and predict what a predicate on the mapped values would test. You may trace it without a Kotlin compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: The function `filter` keeps items that pass a true-or-false rule, called a predicate. The `%` symbol gives the remainder after division. The rule `n % 2 == 0` keeps even numbers because they divide by 2 with no remainder.
The function `map` turns each kept item into a result. Here, its lambda multiplies each number by 10. On this List, filter finishes before map begins; the work does not wait for a later read.
The screen shows `[20, 40]`. Filter keeps 2 and 4. Map then turns them into 20 and 40.
These calls build result lists without changing the original list's numbers. The result has a read-only List view. That view alone does not guarantee that every object inside a list can never change.
